who: American social historian at USC, 1960–1969; PhD Minnesota, 1959.

evidence.says: CV lists the Minnesota PhD, 1954–1959, USC history appointment, 1960–1969, and subsequent Boston University appointment.
Authority for Joseph Boskin identifies the author of Rebellious Laughter as a Boston University history professor and scholar of humor and American culture.

notes: Doctorate and USC appointment agree with the AHA record and all three student years.

who: Modern European intellectual historian at Boston College since 2010; PhD Berkeley, 2001.

who: Daniel A. Cohen, historian of early American culture at Case Western Reserve since 2004; PhD Brandeis, 1989.

evidence.says: Institutional CV identifies Daniel A. Cohen, PhD in History of American Civilization at Brandeis in February 1989; Case Western associate professor from 2004, previously at Florida International University.
Faculty page identifies the Case Western historian and lists Pillars of Salt, Monuments of Grace and The Female Marine and Related Works.
Daniel A. Cohen authority cites Pillars of Salt, Monuments of Grace and The Female Marine and identifies his earlier Florida International history appointment.
The alternative Daniel Jared Cohen authority identifies a George Mason historian and coauthor of Digital History.

notes: Matches Daniel A. Cohen (p-112383); Daniel J. Cohen (p-102159) is a different historian.

who: Early modern French historian at the University of Toronto since 2005; PhD Princeton.

evidence.says: Toronto identifies Paul Cohen as an early modern French historian with a Princeton PhD who joined its faculty in 2005.
Paul A. Cohen authority identifies a Wellesley historian of China with a Harvard PhD, distinct from the Toronto supervisor.
Paula Marantz Cohen is a Drexel English professor with a Columbia English literature PhD (1981).
The candidate authority cites Piety and Politics (1987) under Paul M. Cohen.
Lawrence identifies the author of Piety and Politics as its faculty member from 1985, with a University of Chicago history PhD.
Paul T. Cohen authority identifies a senior lecturer in anthropology and comparative sociology at Macquarie University.

notes: None of the four candidates matches: p-1885 is the Wellesley China historian; p-110351 the Drexel English scholar; p-35119 the Lawrence historian; p-148118 the Macquarie anthropologist.

who: Historian of modern Germany and memory at the University of Virginia; history PhD Berkeley, 1992 (CV).

evidence.says: Confino’s CV lists Virginia history appointments from 1992, promotion to full professor in 2006, a Berkeley history PhD in 1992, and The Nation as a Local Metaphor.
His August 2012 CV confirms the Virginia professorship and Berkeley PhD in 1992.
Alon Confino authority cites The Nation as a Local Metaphor (1997) and The Work of Memory (2002).

notes: Virginia career and publications establish the match. Both CVs give 1992, one year earlier than the AHA doctorate record.

who: Emory G. Evans, colonial American historian and professor emeritus at Maryland, College Park.

evidence.says: The Smithfield Review editor identifies Richard Osborn’s 1990 Maryland dissertation, William Preston 1729–1783: The Making of a Frontier Elite, and names his advisor as Emory Evans.

Emory G. Evans authority identifies a Maryland, College Park history professor emeritus specializing in colonial America; cites The Nelsons: A Biographical Study of a Virginia Family (1957) and A Topping People (2009).

notes: Direct confirmation of listed student Osborn and the candidate’s Maryland affiliation establishes the match.

who: David Frank, Canadian labour and Atlantic Canadian historian at UNB, 1980–2015; PhD Dalhousie.

evidence.says: UNB’s history faculty list includes David Frank, PhD Dalhousie, with appointment year 1980.
The scholarly journal’s retirement tribute records Frank’s 35-year UNB career ending in 2015 and doctoral supervision; Tim Lewis names him as his supervisor.
Review essay footnote 34 identifies David Frank’s The Cape Breton Coal Miners, 1917–1926 as a Dalhousie PhD thesis, 1979.
David Frank authority identifies the contributor to Atlantic Canada Before Confederation (1985) and its companion volume (1999).

notes: Name, regional field, Dalhousie doctorate and UNB career spanning the student years agree.

who: Public and environmental historian at UMass Amherst, 1986–2023; PhD Johns Hopkins, 1982.

evidence.says: UMass identifies Glassberg as professor emeritus, with Johns Hopkins PhD in 1982, and author of American Historical Pageantry and Sense of History.
CV gives UMass history service, 1986–2023, emeritus from 2023, and Johns Hopkins PhD in 1982.
David Glassberg authority cites American Historical Pageantry (1990) and identifies its author as a UMass Amherst history professor.
